tone.voice: a brilliant engineer who communicates clearly — no hype, just capability
tone.avoid: hype-heavy, buzzword-laden, overly casual, corporate fluff

trust_signals: API response time and performance metrics
open source or transparent model info
ux_norms: dark mode is the primary and default mode
dense information layouts are acceptable — users are technical
code blocks and syntax highlighting required
streaming output (typewriter effect) for AI responses
token and usage counters always visible

visual_language.style: abstract geometric — neural network patterns, gradient meshes, data visualisation
photography_rules: no photography on core product screens
real team photos only on about/marketing pages
never use generic tech stock photos (server rooms, handshakes)
visual_language.background_treatment: deep dark — near black with subtle gradient or glow. CSS-driven depth.
visual_language.empty_state_style: minimal abstract SVG — neural node, terminal cursor, or geometric shape with precise copy
visual_language.onboarding_visual: animated geometric SVG or abstract gradient illustration
visual_language.illustration_style: abstract geometric — neural nets, data flows, gradient meshes — never cartoon

compliance_notes: data training opt-out must be clear

avoid: Never use warm photography or human lifestyle imagery in core product screens — SVG and data viz only
Never use decorative gradients or mesh backgrounds — technical aesthetic demands flat precision
Never use casual or playful language in error messages — precise technical language always
Never claim AI capabilities that cannot be demonstrated in the product itself
Never show an AI 'thinking' animation longer than 2 seconds before first token appears
Never use dark patterns to obscure token usage, rate limits, or API costs
enforce: Model name and version always visible to user — never hidden
Data privacy and no-training guarantees surfaced on every data input screen
API documentation link always one click away from any API-related screen
Rate limit status always visible before user hits the limit — not after
Code blocks always syntax highlighted — never plain text
Latency and performance metrics shown honestly — no cherry-picked benchmarks
